rationale.conceptual: The method combines first-principles DFT (PBE, SOC, DOS extraction) with analytical formulas from BCS/Orlando theory. It requires understanding of electronic structure, free-electron model, and superconducting phenomenology. This is an established but non-trivial method that must be applied correctly, placing it at level 3.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of only two sequential steps: a DFT calculation on a known crystal structure (using well-defined inputs) and a script to compute derived quantities. There are no complex dependencies or multi-tool orchestration, and the environment can be prepared with standard DFT packages. Thus, engineering complexity is low (2).

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires a standard DFT calculation with spin-orbit coupling followed by analytic derivation of superconducting parameters using well-known formulas. The conceptual difficulty is moderate (3) because it involves non-trivial condensed-matter physics and careful implementation of a multi-step method, but no novel algorithms. The execution is straightforward (2) with only two main stages: DFT run and post-processing; the pipeline is simple and uses standard tools. Resource needs are minimal (CPU-only, small memory, no large data) as the system is small.
